newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: C&W to sink roots deeper in Asia.
newsitem.headline: C&W to sink roots deeper in Asia.

text.p: Richard Brown, chief executive of British telecommunications giant Cable and Wireless Plc said on Sunday the company plans to deepen its investment roots in Asia and did not discount future mergers.
"This is a recipe of a formula we think is a winning combination," Brown told Reuters at an interview.
Brown was referring to the merger which will bring together C&W's Mercury, British cable company Videotron, Bell Cablemedia and NYNEX CableComms, making it Britain's largest cable operator.
He said C&W sought to replicate the merger, which would enhance C&W's role as an integrated telecommunications, entertainment and information service provider, in South East Asia.

"We are all about being the most global telecoms company in the world, working to get more and more focus in the major markets we serve," Brown said. "We are sinking our roots deeper into the Asian market."
Asia Pacific generates about 70 percent of the group's operating profit, most notably in Hong Kong, where its largest business Hong Kong Telecommunications is found.
Brown said the company was seeking more opportunities in the region and the opening of the Singapore office on Monday, which he would officiate, is a testament to that drive.
He said C&W would use the Singapore office to build on existing partnership and support new investments in the region.

According to C&W's chairman for Asia Pacific development board, Rodney Olsen, the group has invested over the past three to four years about US$1 billion in expansions and new businesses in South East Asia and the Pacific region.
C&W, together with HK Telecom, are partners in Singapore's MobileOne consortium which is building the island state's second cellular communications network.
Olsen said the company's preference was to develop and invest more in countries where C&W already has a presence like Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines.
The company hopes to conclude two-year-long talks on investment prospects in Vietnam "before the beginning of 1997". C&W was among five companies picked to install cables in Hanoi.
Brown took in his stride Sunday's news about the merger of rival British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp.
"I think the winners of the future will not be the bigger players but the better players," Brown said, adding he was happy with the course C&W is undertaking.
